TOP OF BOOK

  • FOMC / WARSH (MACRO) [DELTA ▲] — Fed holds at 3.50–3.75% (6th consecutive hold) but 30yr UST surges 12bp to 5.21%, highest since 2007, while 2yr falls 4bp; 3 dissents favour a hike.
    • Vs. baseline: The hold at 3.50%–3.75% was achieved with roughly a 35% probability of a hike priced ahead of the decision — so the hold itself is not the surprise. What is new: investors sharply lowered the probability of the Fed raising rates at its next meeting but simultaneously raised yields on long-term government debt; after the press conference, the 30-year Treasury hit its highest level since 2007, while the 2-year fell. Three presidents — Hammack (Cleveland), Kashkari (Minneapolis), and Logan (Dallas) — dissented in favour of a quarter-point hike, the most hawkish dissent count since September 2016. Warsh stated the Fed will raise rates if inflation continues to rise and confirmed there is "no soft inflation target."
    • Read: The bear-steepening signal is the key transmission. The 2s30s UST curve blowing out with a hold-but-hawkish read means: (a) NII on floating-rate assets supported short-term but funding costs / deposit betas will reprice; (b) US long-duration rate vol spills into Bund/Gilt term premium — watch whether OAT/BTP spreads widen as the risk-free rate re-anchors higher; (c) European banks with large US operations (Barclays IB, UBS GWM, HSBC) face mark-to-market drag on their US fixed-income books. The Warsh no-forward-guidance regime means September is genuinely live on both sides. Leg: credit (senior/T2, funding cost); Equity: mild negative on high-duration insurers/LDI. Action: MONITOR September ECB/BoE/Fed meetings simultaneously; hedge duration if not already done.
    • Sources: CNBC FOMC live, CNN Fed decision, Axios
  • BRENT CRUDE / MIDDLE EAST (MACRO) [DELTA ▲] — Brent spiked ~7% intraday to ~$89/bbl on 29 July on fresh Iranian attacks on US forces; Strait of Hormuz disruption ongoing since late February 2026.
    • Vs. baseline: Iran launched attacks targeting US troops, which the US military intercepted. Iran-backed militias launched drones at Saudi oil facilities in the Eastern Region for a second consecutive day. Iran rejected Oman's proposal for shared Strait of Hormuz control. Brent had been at ~$87.53 on 28 July and is up ~18% over the past month. The 52-week high was $120.88 in April.
    • Read: A sustained Brent >$90 re-opens second-round wage effects and removes the ECB September cut from the table — NII trajectory for Eurozone banks becomes more supportive for longer, but credit quality deteriorates (energy-intensive corporate SMEs, consumer). Key transmission: BTP-Bund spread widens on stagflation fear for Italy; EM IG/HY credit spreads widen. Energy sector credit (IG) supported. Higher-for-longer rates compress funding relief for leveraged borrowers, widening HY spreads. Action: MONITOR; long Eurozone bank NII beneficiary names (BARC, UCG) vs. short duration / long credit risk protection in consumer-facing names.
    • Sources: Trading Economics Brent, BBVA Research ECB
  • BANK OF ENGLAND (BoE / TODAY) [IN LINE] — BoE MPC decision due 12:00 UK time today (30 July), accompanied by new Monetary Policy Report and Governor's press conference.
    • Vs. baseline: Economists expect a majority to hold at 3.75%. As of 22 July, markets were pricing in two rate hikes by March next year. The prior vote was 7–2 in June, with Megan Greene and Huw Pill dissenting for a hike to 4%. Renewed Middle East-driven energy price pressure has partially offset the near-term inflation easing seen during the US–Iran ceasefire lull, while services inflation at 3.7% keeps a hike on the table.
    • Read: A hold is the base — de-risked, not priced-moving. But the vote split matters enormously: a third hawkish dissenter would be market-moving for Gilts and GBP. The MPR's revised inflation and GDP forecasts are the real information event — if the BoE marks up near-term CPI materially on oil, it validates the market's two-hike path. A hawkish hold reprices the UK yield curve steeper, compressing UK mortgage spreads and weighing on UK bank NII tailwind via deposit beta acceleration; GBP strengthens on rate-differential narrowing vs. EUR. Leg: Gilts (duration risk), GBP (hawkish hold = GBP positive), Barclays UK NII outlook. Action: DIG IN at 12:00 — watch vote split and MPR inflation forecasts vs. prior.
    • Sources: Bank of England, ITV/Reuters

BY NAME / THEME — PRIMARY (EU)

  • BARCLAYS (BARC / BCS) [DELTA ▲] — Q2 PBT +31% YoY to £3.3bn; income £8.3bn (+16%); RoTE 16.1%; full-year income target raised to £31.5bn; £1bn buyback + £800m dividend announced; CET1 14.3%.
    • Vs. baseline: Income of £8.34bn was up 16% from £7.19bn; profit before tax increased 31% to £3.25bn, exceeding the company-compiled consensus estimate of £3.12bn. The bank raised its 2026 income target to approximately £31.5bn and announced £1bn in share buybacks and an £800m interim dividend, bringing H1 distributions to £2.3bn. EPS miss vs. US analyst consensus ($0.23 vs. $0.82 [est.]) was a GAAP/IFRS accounting artefact on the ADS — do not read as economic miss. Q2 impairment charge of £571m equated to a loan loss rate of 51bps. Guidance: LLR "around the top of 50–60bps" for 2026 — no deterioration from Q1.
    • Read: The print closes the MFS overhang thesis: the £228m Q1 MFS charge is already provisioned; Q2 shows no additional MFS credit hits. UK Corporate Bank loans +12% YoY and investment bank equities up 44% confirm structural franchise improvement, not just cyclical trading. Key risk tail: the Rosen Law Firm investigation alleging misleading disclosures around MFS exposure is ongoing — this is a contingent liability, not yet filed as formal complaint; no provision taken. Securities class action risk is primarily an equity tail (litigation discount), not a credit leg event — no capital impact at this stage. Leg: equity positive (guidance upgrade, buyback). Credit: AT1/T2 stable — CET1 at 14.3% (14.0% pro forma for buyback) comfortably above MDA. Litigation: monitor class action status. Action: ADD equity on dips post-Fed vol; credit NO ACTION.
    • Sources: BigGo earnings summary, Pulse2, Rosen Law class action
  • UBS (UBS) [DELTA ▲] — Q2 net profit $2.8bn (+17% YoY); underlying RoCET1 16.4%; new $3bn buyback programme through mid-2027; CET1 14.4%.
    • Vs. baseline: Net profit comfortably exceeded the $2.39bn S&P Global Visible Alpha estimate. The bank has realised $12.6bn of its $13.5bn gross Credit Suisse cost savings target. A new $3bn share buyback programme was announced, running through mid-2027, with at least $1bn expected over the next three months. Equities traders generated 53% more revenue year-on-year, hitting over $2.3bn for a second consecutive quarter.
    • Vs. Swiss capital tail: The Swiss parliamentary committee aims to reach a decision next month; if adopted, the bill could reach the upper house in September with final rules possible by end-2026. The government proposed ~$20bn in additional CET1, but lawmakers may reduce this amount. The pace of future buybacks will depend on UBS maintaining a CET1 ratio of around 14% and further visibility on the Swiss Parliament's deliberations. UBS published a 28-page lobbying document alongside results — an unusually aggressive public move to shape the legislative outcome.
    • Read: The integration story is essentially complete; the earnings power is clear; the binary is the Swiss capital bill. If parliament reduces the $20bn CET1 demand — which committee dynamics suggest is likely — UBS has significant re-rating potential, as the current discount prices in near-worst case. Integration costs remain ~CHF 750m in H2, which will continue to depress reported EPS vs. underlying. US wealth advisor attrition (~$28bn AuM in departures H1) is a longer-term drag but not yet structurally threatening given $36bn NNA. Higher UST long-end rates (per FOMC item) create mark-to-market headwinds on UBS GWM's US fixed-income inventory, compressing NII on reinvestment. Leg: equity — positive on buyback/integration completion; credit — AT1/T2 stable, CET1 well-above requirement. Action: MONITOR Swiss parliament August committee decision (binary for both equity and AT1 buyback pacing).
    • Sources: Investing.com, Global Banking & Finance/Reuters, UBS regulatory statement
  • DEUTSCHE BANK (DBK) [DELTA ▲] — Q2 revenues €8.5bn (+9% YoY); H1 post-tax profit €4.1bn (record); NII guidance raised to "above €14bn"; new €500m buyback announced post completion of current €1bn.
    • Vs. baseline: Investment Bank revenue rose 19% YoY, driven by record Q2 FICC and a 36% increase in IBCM. CET1 ratio 13.9% at end Q2 2026, down from 14.2% a year ago — modest compression from RWA growth (+8% YoY). DBK received supervisory approval for the €500m second buyback, to be executed in H2 2026. Shares finished slightly lower on the day despite the record result — the market had well-anticipated the beat.
    • Read: CET1 drift down to 13.9% is worth watching — if RWA growth continues at +8% on loan growth (+4%) and business mix shift, the headroom to MDA shrinks. That is the key credit-side monitor. FICC strength is broadly in line with peers (Barclays, UBS) — not idiosyncratic alpha. The NII guidance lift to >€14bn (from prior ~€13.6bn guided) is the most valuable data point — confirms deposit repricing and loan volume running above expectations, with higher UST/Bund long rates supporting reinvestment yields on the securities book. Leg: equity neutral-to-positive (already priced). AT1: stable, CET1 buffer comfortable. Action: MONITOR CET1 vs. MDA headroom quarterly; no trade today.
    • Sources: Investing.com transcript, Yahoo Finance highlights
  • EUROBANK (EUROB.AT) — TODAY [IN LINE] — Q2 2026 results announced today after Athens market close (6pm local); conference call same evening.
    • Vs. baseline: Citi expects underlying net profit of €377m (before minority interests and AT1 coupon), representing +8% QoQ and +4% YoY. Buyback ongoing — recent tranche at €3.33/share vs. current ~€4.41 (52-week range €3.12–€4.51). A beat on NII vs. consensus would be the alpha signal given rising energy-driven rate expectations.
    • Read: Greek banks are NII-duration long; a higher-for-longer ECB rate path — now live given the Middle East energy shock — is a positive surprise for 2027 NII, directly expanding net interest margin on variable-rate loan books and delaying deposit repricing pressure. The key figures to watch are NPE trajectory and cost of risk — not the headline profit. Action: DIG IN at close today; any Q3 NII guidance upgrade on ECB expectations is equity-positive and tightens EUROB sub-debt spreads.
    • Sources: Cyprus Mail/Citi, Yahoo Finance
  • BARCLAYS / MFS / PRIVATE CREDIT READ-THROUGH [IN LINE] — No additional MFS provisions in Q2; MFS administration and FCA probe ongoing.
    • Vs. baseline: Barclays took a £228m hit in Q1 tied to the collapse of MFS, overshadowing an otherwise solid trading quarter. HSBC reported a $400m impairment from MFS in its Q1 results; Santander's exposure is understood at ~$267m. The debacle exposes structural risks around double-pledging and counterparty risk within complex credit structures — a theme that has not resolved.
    • Read: The sector read-through is for structured finance / specialty lending warehouse facilities at other European banks. The FCA enforcement investigation into MFS is live. Apollo/Atlas SP Partners exposure (part of the >£2bn loan pool) means the private credit <> bank interface story is not closed. This is a slow-moving systemic credit story — the risk is not priced back in. Barclays management explicitly flagged it is "constraining lending to certain structured finance counterparties who operate more vulnerable business models," tightening funding availability and widening spreads on warehouse facilities across the sector. Watch for similar tightening disclosures from HSBC and Santander in H2. Action: MONITOR; screen for other EU bank specialty-lending/warehouse exposures in upcoming prints.
    • Sources: Banking Exchange, CNBC
  • UNICREDIT (UCG) / COMMERZBANK (CBK) M&A [IN LINE] — UCG reported record Q2 net profit €3.1bn (22nd consecutive record quarter); shares fell ~5% on Commerzbank execution risk concerns.
    • Vs. baseline: Despite record profit and raised full-year guidance, shares fell 4.91%, reflecting investor concerns about execution risk related to the Commerzbank acquisition strategy and capital allocation priorities. UCG now expects 2028 net profit well above €13bn and 2030 net profit exceeding €15bn, contingent on Commerzbank integration.
    • Read: The market is pricing integration premium risk — not fundamental deterioration. This is a positioning opportunity if the Commerzbank deal closes on manageable terms. UCG's standalone earnings trajectory (NII stabilising, loan growth +8% YoY) is the floor; higher-for-longer ECB rates extend NII support and underpin the standalone valuation case. Action: MONITOR Commerzbank regulatory/political clearance news; UCG equity: the entry thesis is improving on this weakness.
    • Sources: Investing.com
  • BNP PARIBAS (BNP) [DELTA ▲] — Q2 revenue +12% YoY to €12.2bn; net profit +33% to €3.0bn (includes €858m Ageas/AGI capital gain); cost of risk 39bps; jaws positive.
    • Vs. baseline: BNP reported strong Q2 results, with group revenue rising 12% year-on-year to €12.2bn; operating income rose nearly 16% to €4.1bn, while net profit increased one-third to €3.0bn, boosted by the Ageas/AGI capital gain. Cost of risk remained stable at 39bps, within the through-the-cycle guidance of below 40bps, with an additional €95m geopolitical provision.
    • Sources: BNP Paribas investor relations
